nodes.label: Exact-Match Rule (Anti-Phishing)
nodes.rationale: If the UPI or bank details in an email do not match the stored record for that sender, the system never auto-pays and marks the item needs_approval with a 'Changed Details' flag.

nodes.label: Idempotency Key (Zero Double Payment)
nodes.rationale: Each email and payment gets a unique idempotency_key = sha256(message_id + amount + payee); the database uniqueness rule blocks the second attempt if a cron or button fires twice. If any uniqueness constraint is missing, the double-payment tests (T-18..T-22) will eventually fail.

nodes.label: x402 Service Marketplace
nodes.rationale: Every service is probe-verified before listing and priced before payment, so a bad or misbehaving service costs at most the per-call price it quoted - cents, not the budget.

nodes.label: Perflo AP Agent
nodes.rationale: A queue, not a chatbot: CFO teams want to see the triggers, the steps and the failures, with an agent handling the smart parts in between. 'I want an agent, not an app' - a database, a worker with cron jobs, an LLM agent with tools for judgement, deterministic code for everything that touches money.

nodes.label: Classifier
nodes.rationale: Cheap code pass drops obvious noise first; the LLM then sorts the rest with no tools, so an injected instruction in the body cannot steer it. Untrusted content sits inside delimiters in the prompt.

nodes.label: Extractor
nodes.rationale: Sandboxed (no tools), structured JSON output only with a confidence per field. Free text from a model never becomes a parameter to Perflo.

nodes.label: Perflo Grant Guardrail
nodes.rationale: The owner approves each payee once in their own browser with caps (per payment, total, count, expiry). Even if every LLM in the system is fooled, money can only go to a recipient the owner approved, up to those caps. Don't design anything that routes around it - there is no 'pay to arbitrary VPA' path.

nodes.label: Ingest Worker
nodes.rationale: Dedupe on gmail_message_id so a message is ingested once, ever. Composio triggers get missed, so polling has to exist anyway.

nodes.label: Notifier
nodes.rationale: Approval emails come from the app's own sender, never the owner's Gmail, and carry one signed single-use link - no approve button in the email itself, and no payment details an attacker would want to learn.

nodes.label: Payee Resolver
nodes.rationale: Exact-match rule: auto-pay only if the sender identity maps to an approved payee AND the extracted payment-details hash equals the stored approved method. 'This one rule kills most business email compromise on its own.' Mappings are never inferred; they exist only because the owner approved them.

nodes.label: Payment Executor
nodes.rationale: Idempotency key (sha256 of message, payee method, amount, currency, reference) enforced by a unique index, and a single writer per intent via row locks. Unknown outcome means 'assume it was sent' until the reconciler proves otherwise. The owner's two failure modes - an agent that pays twice inside guardrails - are what this component exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Policy Engine
nodes.rationale: The money decision is deterministic code, never an LLM: auto_pay only when all FR-19 checks hold (classification, extraction confidence, exact payee match, auth, verifier score, no duplicate, grant caps, ceiling, not paused). The LLM never executes money directly.

nodes.label: Anti-Prompt Injection Controls
nodes.rationale: The LLM extractor is sandboxed (no tools) and parses the email inside delimiters; the system flags the injection and moves the email to quarantined. Structured output only; injection snippets must appear in the evidence.

nodes.label: Queue UI
nodes.rationale: Business owners and CFOs want a table/queue - Queued, Needs Approval, Auto-Paid, Quarantined, Duplicate - not a chatbot. A chat box can come last, if at all.

nodes.label: Reconciler
nodes.rationale: Resolves paying/unknown_outcome/paid intents from perflo activity and tx status. Never re-pays anything.

nodes.label: Verifier
nodes.rationale: Invoice fraud is the single most common way businesses lose money; any AP automation that pays what it reads is a machine for losing money faster. The verifier is not a feature on top - it is the reason this thing is safe to run unattended. It returns an evidence bundle and never decides to pay.

nodes.label: x402 Protocol
nodes.rationale: Invoice links are opened only in Perflo's x402 headless browser - a clean, paid, isolated session where the vendor eats the risk of rendering attacker-controlled pages. The browser output stays untrusted. Never open a link with the app's own fetch or the owner's browser session.

nodes.label: Money
nodes.rationale: The amount travels as a decimal string rather than as a JSON number so no precision is lost in transit.

nodes.label: OperationView
nodes.rationale: Every financial write stores this record and its idempotency record before the write is submitted, so there is always something to poll.

nodes.label: QuoteView
nodes.rationale: A quote is never executable on its own: POST /v1/transfers spends it, and it carries a confirm_by deadline after which it is refused rather than repriced.

nodes.label: TransferCreate
nodes.rationale: The beneficiary and every amount come from the named quote rather than from this request body, so a stale quote is refused rather than repriced.

nodes.label: POST /v1/operations/{operation_id}/approval/poll
nodes.rationale: Approval polling is intentionally repeatable and takes no idempotency key; the original mutation is never resubmitted while approval is outstanding.

nodes.label: isDefinitiveNoOperation
nodes.rationale: A definitive no-operation result proves the write never landed, so a replacement operation is safe; every other result requires the documented recovery policy.

nodes.label: isProblemDetails
nodes.rationale: The error field is unknown because it can hold a problem document, a decode failure or a network error, so isProblemDetails is required before reading problem codes.

nodes.label: Operation lifecycle tracking
nodes.rationale: Every financial mutation records an idempotent operation before submission, so there is always something to poll and a lost response is never blindly repeated.

nodes.label: Problem document (application/problem+json)
nodes.rationale: code is the stable machine-readable branch key; title and detail are human text that must not be branched on.

nodes.label: Perflo MCP Connector
nodes.rationale: Agents get a permission slip via OAuth, never the account keys: the connector never sees or stores the Perflo password, reads never need approval, and the access can be revoked anytime.

nodes.label: Machine-Readable Error Codes
nodes.rationale: Denials are final for that request and always logged; the agent receives a stable machine-readable code with the limit and amount, so a well-built agent can explain exactly why it stopped and adjust.

nodes.label: Kill Switch
nodes.rationale: One tap in the app instantly cuts off every agent's access, even mid-task. Nothing pending survives it, and nothing resumes on its own.

nodes.label: Agent Guardrail Session (Budget)
nodes.rationale: A budget is a hard ceiling that never refills itself. Cumulative caps count money still in flight, so concurrent or rapid-fire requests cannot race past a cap together.

nodes.label: Perflo Docs: Agent Spending and Budgets
nodes.norm_label: perflo docs: agent spending and budgets

nodes.label: AgentPairingView
nodes.rationale: A self-asserted agent name is never verified, so verified is always false.

nodes.label: MandateView
nodes.rationale: A beneficiary mandate's remaining allowance counts only payments made under the mandate, making it an upper bound on what the backing Perflo grant can still spend.

nodes.label: MandateRevocationBatchView
nodes.rationale: The batch names the revocations it opened rather than their outcomes because each mandate revocation carries its own state and settles independently.

nodes.label: Fees and limits policy
nodes.rationale: The confirmation screen always shows the full cost before approval; if no cost is shown, there is none.

nodes.label: Agent spending allowance
nodes.rationale: Kept as a separate capped guardrail surface so the worst an agent can do is spend its allowance on already-approved services; customer wealth stays untouched.

nodes.label: Guardrails safety layer
nodes.rationale: Checks run before any approval exists and fail closed: if Perflo cannot determine the dollar value of a request, the request is denied.

nodes.label: Kill switch (agent revocation)
nodes.rationale: Revocation is fail-closed: access is shut down first, and if any step of confirming the shutdown cannot complete, access stays revoked and an alert fires.

nodes.label: Public venue routing
nodes.rationale: Perflo runs no exchange and never takes the other side of a trade, so prices, rates and liquidity come from the public venues and are passed through.

nodes.label: Self-custodial smart account
nodes.rationale: Perflo does not hold assets in an omnibus company wallet and cannot move money by itself, so balances are verifiable on public block explorers.

nodes.label: Session permissions
nodes.rationale: Withdrawals to external addresses always require a fresh confirmation and no session can raise its own limits, so money can never leave the account without the customer.

nodes.label: POST /cli/token/refresh
nodes.rationale: Refresh is not idempotent because the refresh token can rotate when spent, so the stored accessJwt, refreshToken and expiresAt are replaced atomically only after every check succeeds.

nodes.label: POST /v1/perflo-connections/current/poll
nodes.rationale: This route has no idempotency key because completion retires the one-time link session; onboarding is the recovery source of truth after a lost poll response.

nodes.label: OperationView
nodes.rationale: Every financial write stores the operation record and its idempotency record before the write is submitted, so there is always something to poll.

nodes.label: Start a card reveal session (POST /v1/cards/{card_id}/reveal-sessions)
nodes.rationale: A card number is never proxied or returned, URLs outside the trusted Perflo origin are refused, and no operation is recorded.

nodes.label: Unfreeze a card (POST /v1/cards/{card_id}/unfreeze)
nodes.rationale: A confirmed failure restores the previous status; a transport-uncertain write leaves the card and operation indeterminate and is never repeated, so a client must stop before the replay window ends and reconcile history rather than retry.

nodes.label: Withdraw card-account funds (POST /v1/card-account/withdrawals)
nodes.rationale: The Idempotency-Key binds for the replay window so equal replays return the same operation; a transport-uncertain write is never repeated automatically.

nodes.label: Create a confirmation intent (POST /v1/confirmation-intents)
nodes.rationale: The intent is one-use, bound to the normalized payload of the named action, and expires ten minutes after creation.

nodes.label: CardView
nodes.rationale: last4 is the only fragment of the card number ever published, and indeterminate records a transport-uncertain write that is never repeated automatically.

nodes.label: NonNegativeMoney
nodes.rationale: Amount travels as a decimal string rather than a JSON number so no precision is lost in transit.

nodes.label: CardDepositAddressView
nodes.rationale: The full deposit address is readable only with the linked customer's own token.

nodes.label: Money
nodes.rationale: Amount travels as a decimal string rather than a JSON number so no precision is lost in transit.

nodes.label: Read a card (GET /v1/cards/{card_id})
nodes.rationale: Answers synchronously from the card's stored state so a read cannot overwrite a write that is in flight.

nodes.label: GET /v1/activity
nodes.rationale: The route merges and deduplicates two activity sources and is customer-wide, not a per-account ledger, so entries must not be attributed to an account.

nodes.label: GET /v1/display-currency
nodes.rationale: A null response means no display conversion applies; the rate is an indicative display aid, not an executable quote.

nodes.label: GET /v1/kyc
nodes.rationale: KYC status is intentionally absent from onboarding; GET /v1/kyc is its single source.

nodes.label: Handoff Nonce
nodes.rationale: The frame signs a caller-selected message automatically and is an origin-isolation boundary, not a user-consent boundary; a relying service can attach consequences to a valid EIP-191 signature, so message selection is authority.

nodes.label: Hyperliquid
nodes.rationale: Hyperliquid is one of the public venues Perflo routes to for trading.

nodes.label: Morpho
nodes.rationale: Morpho vaults back Earn balances; Perflo routes to these public protocols that exist independently of Perflo.

nodes.label: Perflo
nodes.rationale: Perflo positions itself as a compliant money platform (MSB) rather than a bank; assets are self-custodial, explaining why balances are not deposit-insured.

nodes.label: Polymarket
nodes.rationale: Polymarket is one of the public venues for prediction markets.

nodes.label: USDC
nodes.rationale: Cash balances are held as USDC issued by Circle, which holds reserves against it.

nodes.label: External withdrawal confirmation
nodes.rationale: Withdrawals to external addresses always require the user; agents cannot perform them.

nodes.label: Base network
nodes.rationale: Base (chain ID 8453) is the primary network for accounts, deposits, Earn, and agent x402 payments.

nodes.label: Ethereum network (legacy)
nodes.rationale: Ethereum is used only for legacy accounts opened before the move to Base.

nodes.label: Hyperliquid network
nodes.rationale: Hyperliquid runs its own L1 chain used for futures trading and margin.

nodes.label: Morpho on Ethereum contract
nodes.rationale: Morpho lending/vault protocol on Ethereum, for legacy accounts.

nodes.label: Morpho vaults
nodes.rationale: Three named public Morpho vaults are the venues Earn can deposit into, all on Base.

nodes.label: Polygon network
nodes.rationale: Polygon (chain ID 137) hosts Polymarket prediction trading with USDC settlement.

nodes.label: Perflo smart account
nodes.rationale: A Perflo account is a smart account the user controls on public blockchains, verifiable via explorers.

nodes.label: USDC.e on Polygon contract
nodes.rationale: Polygon USDC used by Polymarket for prediction market settlement.

nodes.label: Permission limits and expiry
nodes.rationale: Every permission that moves funds has limits and an expiry; no permission can raise its own limits.

nodes.label: Smart account custody
nodes.rationale: No seed phrase; keys are protected inside infrastructure Perflo cannot read, and Perflo cannot move money on its own.

nodes.label: USDC stablecoin
nodes.rationale: Balance is held in USDC; incoming stablecoins convert straight into the balance.

nodes.label: USDT stablecoin
nodes.rationale: USDT can be deposited and is converted to USDC on arrival rather than bounced.

nodes.label: Local virtual accounts
nodes.rationale: Named virtual accounts with local details for receiving first- and third-party payments.

nodes.label: Position exit
nodes.rationale: Positions can be closed partially or fully at any time; closing is never locked; free margin can be withdrawn.

nodes.label: Hedge protection
nodes.rationale: Optional feature for Ethereum accounts holding spot assets; maintains a short futures position sized against holding, reducing downside but capping upside.

nodes.label: Leverage and margin
nodes.rationale: Leverage multiplies gains and losses; margin posted in USDC; app shows liquidation price as leverage adjusts.

nodes.label: Perpetual futures
nodes.rationale: Futures on Perflo are perpetual contracts executed on Hyperliquid; trades do not hold underlying assets.

nodes.label: Prediction guardrails
nodes.rationale: Quality controls GUARD_MIN_MARKET_VOLUME and GUARD_MIN_WIN_PROBABILITY filter thin markets and low-probability bets for agents.

nodes.label: Polymarket prediction market
nodes.rationale: Positions execute on Polymarket, the largest prediction market; every market is a question with a defined resolution.

nodes.label: Prediction redemption
nodes.rationale: After a market resolves, winning shares can be redeemed to the balance; positions can also be exited early by selling back to the market.

nodes.label: YES/NO shares
nodes.rationale: Shares priced between $0.00 and $1.00 reflecting probability; winners pay $1.00, losers $0.00.

nodes.label: Bank payouts and saved recipients
nodes.rationale: Automations and agents can only pay recipients that are saved and allowlisted; adding a new recipient always requires the customer.

nodes.label: Virtual Mastercard
nodes.rationale: Agent-created cards load only the amount needed and can be frozen right after use, so an agent can buy from any merchant without ever holding open access to the customer's money.

nodes.label: Agent pfa_ pairing token
nodes.rationale: Revocation or mandate expiry is what ends a copied token's authority, so the mandate's own limits are what a leaked token can actually spend.

nodes.label: Customer Perflo token (EdDSA accessJwt)
nodes.rationale: The token is financial authority over the customer's Perflo account, so it must be kept in a server-side session; browser exposure would let an XSS vulnerability act as the customer.

nodes.label: Gateway device credential
nodes.rationale: Work on the customer's account runs through a separate encrypted device credential so the customer token is never copied into the stored gateway credential slot; the API never returns it.

nodes.label: Identity principal (customer | agent)
nodes.rationale: Every public authenticated request resolves to one immutable principal, which determines which routes can be called and which identity is attributed to each operation.

nodes.label: POST /v1/agent-tokens/refresh
nodes.rationale: The token is never rotated, so a lost refresh response leaves the existing value usable.

nodes.label: ConnectCodeRedemptionView
nodes.rationale: The opaque pairing bearer token is returned only at redemption, so it appears exactly once.

nodes.label: Webhook HMAC signing secret
nodes.rationale: The signing secret is returned only by the creation response and cannot be read again, so rotation is done by replacing the subscription.

nodes.label: max_price Ceiling
nodes.rationale: A natural-language query target only checks max_price immediately before and after the charge, so an overage surfaces after money moves; only a catalogued service or quoted endpoint carries the ceiling into the charge itself.

nodes.label: Webhook Signing Secret
nodes.rationale: The signing secret is returned once and is unrecoverable, so it must be stored immediately in a secret manager; a verified delivery requires HMAC over the exact raw bytes before any JSON parsing.

nodes.label: Confirmation Intent
nodes.rationale: A confirmation intent is payload confirmation, not an independent MFA event: a ten-minute, one-use record bound to one sensitive action and its normalized payload.

nodes.label: Pairing Token (pfa_)
nodes.rationale: A pfa_ token carries no device or network binding and is never rotated, so a copied token is bounded in spending by the mandate's caps and expiry; only pairing revocation and mandate expiry end its authority.

nodes.label: Perflo Finance API
nodes.rationale: Authority boundary: customer Perflo tokens stay server-side and the gateway never returns its stored device credential or card PAN/CVV; agents receive only a mandate-scoped pfa_ token so a leaked agent credential stays bounded by the mandate's caps.

nodes.label: BearerAuth security scheme
nodes.rationale: Accepts a Perflo customer access token or a pfa_ pairing token, as required by the operation.

nodes.label: BeneficiarySchemaView (payout form)
nodes.rationale: Null purpose_codes is advisory; a non-empty list is authoritative and POST /v1/beneficiaries is refused unless purpose_code is one of its values.

nodes.label: BeneficiaryView
nodes.rationale: Every field is always emitted; null means the beneficiary has no value, never that this read omitted it.

nodes.label: CardView
nodes.rationale: A card that has never been funded reads as zero rather than as absent; neither the full card number nor any verification value is ever published.

nodes.label: NonNegativeMoney
nodes.rationale: Amount travels as a decimal string rather than as a JSON number, so no precision is lost in transit.

nodes.label: OperationView
nodes.rationale: Every financial write stores this record and its idempotency record before the write is submitted, so there is always something to poll.

nodes.label: ProblemDetails
nodes.rationale: Carries a stable machine-readable code to branch on, while title and detail are human text that can be reworded.

nodes.label: SignedMoney
nodes.rationale: Card ledger entries carry direction in the amount's sign and have no kind field to move it to, so this is the one signed money shape.

nodes.label: Confirmation-Intent-ID
nodes.rationale: One-use, transaction-bound confirmation.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key
nodes.rationale: Idempotency-Key binds for at least the replay window published by GET /v1/identity; inside that window an equal replay returns the same operation with Idempotent-Replayed set to true.

nodes.label: NonNegativeMoney
nodes.rationale: The amount travels as a decimal string rather than as a JSON number so no precision is lost in transit.

nodes.label: ProblemDetails
nodes.rationale: code is the stable machine-readable identifier to branch on; title and detail are human text and can be reworded, so clients must branch on code.

nodes.label: PurchaseView
nodes.rationale: Price cap enforcement depends on the purchase target: a catalogued service or quoted endpoint caps at charge, while a natural-language query target is only preflight-checked so its ceiling stays advisory at the moment of charge.

nodes.label: BeneficiaryGrantView
nodes.rationale: No reservation ledger is kept and no mandate records the grant, so concurrent spending by another client sharing the account is bounded only by the grant's own caps.

nodes.label: Money
nodes.rationale: The amount travels as a decimal string rather than a JSON number so no precision is lost in transit.

nodes.label: KycView
nodes.rationale: status_changed_at records when the normalized status was observed — a read time — because the moment the status actually changed is not stated.

nodes.label: OnboardingView
nodes.rationale: Verification status is deliberately absent from this view because GET /v1/kyc is its single source.

nodes.label: ConnectCodeView
nodes.rationale: The short-lived selector lets an agent learn its mandate_id without the customer handing over a raw UUID.

nodes.label: ProblemDetails
nodes.rationale: code is the stable machine-readable identifier to branch on; title and detail are human text and can be reworded.

nodes.label: Start card verification (POST /v1/card-account/kyc-sessions)
nodes.rationale: The verification token is a one-session credential, not a reusable customer-account token, and must not be logged or persisted.

nodes.label: Read sign-in branding (GET /v1/public-config)
nodes.rationale: Takes no credential and makes no remote read, and carries no customer or account data, so the sign-in surface can render before anyone authenticates.

nodes.label: Classifier (Fast LLM, No Tools)
nodes.rationale: Cheap deterministic code filter runs before the LLM to drop newsletters, calendar invites, and automated receipts without model spend; untrusted body text is wrapped in delimiters to neutralize prompt injections.

nodes.label: Extractor (LLM, Strict JSON)
nodes.rationale: Enforces a strict JSON output schema with per-field confidence; ambiguous amounts are forced to low confidence so they require manual approval instead of auto-payment.

nodes.label: FR-16 Exact-Match Rule
nodes.rationale: Any change to bank details (e.g. VPA) produces a details_hash UNIQUE mismatch and is flagged as Changed Details -> needs_approval; never auto-paid.

nodes.label: Golden Rule: Deterministic Money, Sandboxed LLM
nodes.rationale: Immutable invariant: the LLM never touches money (classifier and extractor have zero tools, verifier has only read-only x402 tools); payment logic is deterministic TypeScript + PostgreSQL row locks; Perflo browser-approved guardrails are the gate for all money movement.
nodes.norm_label: golden rule: deterministic money, sandboxed llm

nodes.label: x402 Marketplace Tools
nodes.rationale: Paid verifications (verify_email, browse_web) are the only LLM-adjacent spend and are strictly read-only; invoice links opened inside Perflo's isolated headless browser.

nodes.label: Golden Invariant 3: Anti-Phishing / Anti-BEC (FR-16)
nodes.rationale: Any changed bank account / UPI ID triggers a details_hash UNIQUE mismatch and routes to needs_approval with a Changed Details warning.

nodes.label: Golden Invariant 4: Anti-Prompt Injection Defense
nodes.rationale: Classifier and extractor prompts strictly delimited with structured JSON output; suspicious injection text flagged and routed to quarantined.

nodes.label: Golden Invariant 2: Double-Payment Defense
nodes.rationale: Enforced via gmail_message_id UNIQUE, idempotency_key UNIQUE, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, and per-payee in-flight serialization.

nodes.label: Golden Invariant 5: Perflo CLI & Guardrail Integration
nodes.rationale: Payments executed only via perflo recipient pay with interpretation block stored; Perflo browser-approved grants are the immutable money fence.
nodes.norm_label: golden invariant 5: perflo cli & guardrail integration

nodes.label: Golden Invariant 1: Zero LLM Payment Execution
nodes.rationale: LLM strictly sandboxed without payment tools; deterministic TypeScript code + PostgreSQL row locking control payments.
nodes.norm_label: golden invariant 1: zero llm payment execution

nodes.label: Master System & Verification Audit Prompt
nodes.rationale: Purpose is to verify the entire codebase against the v0 PRD (FR-1 to FR-32, T-1 to T-25) and the 5 golden invariants, producing a complete audit report before any further code change.
